title: Test forms on the chart whose pull-back field is a prescribed φ (supplied steps 3–6 and 8; Simon 6.2.35)
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, let ι : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be a linear isometry with adjoint A := ι*, let u : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, δ₁, δ₂ ∈ ℝ and φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1}. Write D := B_{δ₁}(0) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, G(v) := x + ιv + u(v), DG(v) for the Fréchet derivative of G at v, e_0, …, e_n for the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1}, j.succAbove : {0, …, n−1} → {0, …, n} for the increasing enumeration of {0, …, n} ∖ {j}, and Z := {w ∈ ℝ^P : |A(w − x)| < δ₁ and |w − x − ιA(w − x)| < δ₂}. Assume: δ₂ > 0; closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂) ⊆ U; u is differentiable on D; ⟨ιw, u(v)⟩ = 0 for all v ∈ D and w ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; |u(v)| < δ₂/2 for all v ∈ D; φ is C^∞, has compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ D and |φ(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. Then there is a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n: a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U) such that (i) tsupport ω ⊆ Z; (ii) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, δ₁ + δ₂); (iii) covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(w)) ≤ (n+1)!·√(P^n) for every w ∈ ℝ^P; and (iv) φ = 1_D · Σ_{j=0}^{n} (−1)^j ω(G(·))(DG(·)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(·)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}) e_j, i.e. for v ∈ D, φ(v) = Σ_j ((−1)^j ω(G(v))(DG(v)e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, DG(v)e_{j.succAbove(n−1)})) e_j, and φ(v) = 0 for v ∉ D.
